summary.one_liner: ClipMenu is an older clipboard manager for Mac OS X, written in Objective-C, with a Swift rewrite announced as under development.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes ClipMenu as a clipboard manager for Mac OS X. It lists third-party dependencies it relies on: PTHotKey, Shortcut Recorder, Sparkle, DBPrefsWindowController, Google Toolbox for Mac, and BWToolkit. The README gives no detailed feature list. It also says a completely rebuilt version in Swift is under development, with more information to come. The README does not describe the current feature set in detail.
use_cases: keep a history of copied clipboard items on a Mac
access recent clipboard entries from the menu bar
build or modify a Mac OS X clipboard manager
study an older Objective-C macOS menu bar app
how_to_run: Install the listed dependencies (PTHotKey, Shortcut Recorder, Sparkle, DBPrefsWindowController, Google Toolbox for Mac, BWToolkit) before compiling.
Build the source code with Xcode (README targets Xcode 3.2).
notable: Menu bar clipboard manager for Mac OS X
Depends on several third-party macOS libraries, including Sparkle for updates
A Swift rewrite is announced as in development
Permits derived works under the MIT license, with a request not to use the name ClipMenu as a product name
caveats: Targets Mac OS X 10.5 to 10.6 and Xcode 3.2, which are very old platforms
Requires downloading and installing several external libraries before building
The README says the Swift rewrite is under development and gives no release date
